evidence: minisvc/storage/repo.py:17-22 inserts directly into a local SQLite file; each method opens a new connection and there is no backup, migration, or retry layer
impact: Order data durability depends on a single local file and can be fragile in ephemeral or poorly managed runtime environments
mitigation: Define supported deployment storage, add backup/migration guidance, and consider a managed DB or explicit durability procedures

evidence: README.md:8 claims durable audit storage, but minisvc/audit.py:4-10 only returns an event dict and minisvc/storage/repo.py:11-15 creates no audit table
impact: No durable audit trail exists for created or read actions, limiting compliance evidence and post-incident analysis
mitigation: Either implement persisted audit records or remove/replace the claim and document the current ephemeral behavior

evidence: minisvc/config.py:10-14 loads MINISVC_DB and MINISVC_READONLY; minisvc/cli.py:8-11 uses database_path but no runtime code consults Settings.readonly
impact: Runtime behavior does not match configuration expectations, and defaulting to orders.sqlite may place data in an unintended working directory
mitigation: Enforce readonly mode in write paths and document or validate the database file location at startup

evidence: minisvc/api/handlers.py:7-10 accesses payload keys directly and casts total_cents with int(); no try/except or schema validation is present
impact: Malformed requests can raise KeyError or ValueError and bubble up as unstable API failures
mitigation: Add request schema validation and convert validation failures into explicit client-facing error responses

evidence: minisvc/api/routes.py:4-6 assumes app.post and app.get methods, but the repo contains no app factory or framework dependency
impact: Integration can break silently if the host app contract differs, and new engineers have no in-repo runnable HTTP bootstrap
mitigation: Add a documented adapter contract or a concrete app bootstrap module with a smoke test
